record.paper_title: On a general Syracuse problem with conjectures
record.context_brief: Cycle classification for the 3n+5 Syracuse variant
record.original_question: For the map T(n)=n/2 when n is even and T(n)=(3n+5)/2 when n is odd, is C(3,5) exactly the six cycles with least elements 1, 5, 19, 23, 187, and 347, of respective lengths 3, 2, 5, 5, 27, and 27? Equivalently, do the positive integers decompose as N=G(1)∪G(5)∪G(19)∪G(23)∪G(187)∪G(347), with no divergent trajectories G(∞)=∅?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.3. For ν = 2, a = 2ν − 1 = 3 and b = 2ν + 1 = 5 , the set C(a, b ) contains exactly 6 cycles C(a, b ) = { Ω(1), Ω(5), Ω(19), Ω(23), Ω(187), Ω(347)} , and N = G(1) ∪ G(5) ∪ G(19) ∪ G(23) ∪ G(187) ∪ G(347). We have G(∞ ) = ∅ with the cycles of length 3, 2, 5, 5, 27 and 27, respectively,

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the map $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ by
$$T(n)=\begin{cases}n/2 & \text{if }n\text{ is even},\\ (3n+5)/2 & \text{if }n\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}$$
For a positive integer $m$, let $\Omega(m)$ denote a cycle of $T$ whose least element is $m$, and let $G(m)$ denote the set of positive integers whose forward $T$-orbit eventually enters $\Omega(m)$. Let $G(\infty)$ denote the set of positive integers with divergent $T$-orbit (orbit unbounded), and let $\mathcal{C}(3,5)$ be the set of all cycles of $T$ on $\mathbb{N}$.

The following six cycles of $T$ are known:
- $\Omega(1):\ 1\to 4\to 2\to 1$ (length $3$),
- $\Omega(5):\ 5\to 10\to 5$ (length $2$),
- $\Omega(19):\ 19\to 31\to 49\to 76\to 38\to 19$ (length $5$),
- $\Omega(23):\ 23\to 37\to 58\to 29\to 46\to 23$ (length $5$),
- $\Omega(187)$ of length $27$,
- $\Omega(347)$ of length $27$.

Prove or disprove: $\mathcal{C}(3,5)=\{\Omega(1),\Omega(5),\Omega(19),\Omega(23),\Omega(187),\Omega(347)\}$, $G(\infty)=\emptyset$, and consequently
$$\mathbb{N}=G(1)\cup G(5)\cup G(19)\cup G(23)\cup G(187)\cup G(347).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The 3n+5 variant of the Collatz/Syracuse map is a well-known generalized Collatz problem. The six cycles with least elements 1, 5, 19, 23, 187, 347 are documented in the literature, but no proof exists that these are the only cycles or that no divergent trajectory exists. Like the standard Collatz conjecture, this remains an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On Cycles of Generalized Collatz Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: The generalized Collatz function F5 (the 3n+5 variant) contains 6 known cycles including those with least elements 1, 5, 19, 23, 187, 347.
status_evidence.claim: The six cycles are documented but the conjecture that they are the only cycles, with no divergent orbits, remains unproved.

status_evidence.title: Collatz conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations of the Collatz problem, including 3n+k variants, remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The cycle/divergence problem for 3n+5 generalizations of Collatz is open.
